411
FOR-wun-WUN
noun (Gen X slang)
From 4-1-1, long the telephone number for directory assistance in much of the United States: dial it and an operator would look up a listing for you. In African-American speech of the late 1980s the 411 came to mean the information, the facts, the lowdown on a person or situation ("What’s the 411?"), and hip-hop and R&B carried it nationwide; Mary J. Blige named her debut album What’s the 411? (1992). Kin to the older the lowdown, the scoop, and the skinny.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The 411 is the information — who, what, where, and especially the details everyone else does not know yet. The phrase came from the old directory-assistance number and from Black American speech of the late 1980s, and Mary J. Blige made it a household phrase in 1992. "Give me the 411 on the new guy." The Christian observation is that information is good and gossip is not, and the 411 can be either. Scripture prizes careful inquiry: "It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter" (Pro 25:2). It warns against answering too fast: "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him" (Pro 18:13). But it also knows how quickly "the 411 on somebody" becomes the talebearer’s trade: "The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly" (Pro 18:8). Before passing on the 411, ask whether it is true, whether it is mine to tell, and whether it will build up. Best of all, Scripture tells us where the deepest information is found. "For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding" (Pro 2:6). "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally" (Jas 1:5). God even gives out His own number: "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not" (Jer 33:3). A father can teach his children to get the facts straight, keep other people’s secrets, and call the One who has all the 411 and never gossips.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen X slang (late 1980s, from the US directory-assistance number; Black American speech, popularized by Mary J. Blige, 1992) for the information or lowdown; Scripture separates honest inquiry (Pro 18:13) from talebearing (Pro 18:8) and sends the seeker to God for wisdom (Jas 1:5).

411, n. (Gen X slang, late 1980s–1990s, African-American speech) Information; the facts or the inside story about a person or situation. "What’s the 411 on the party Friday?"

From the telephone number 4-1-1, directory assistance; said "four-one-one"; kin to the lowdown, the scoop, the skinny, the dirt.

Popularized by hip-hop and R&B; Mary J. Blige, What’s the 411? (1992).

Webster 1828: INFORM, v.i. To give intelligence. …

Decode for parents: the 411 can be honest inquiry or polished gossip; teach your children to tell the difference before they pass it on.

Key Scripture

Pro 18:13 — "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him."

Pro 18:8 — "The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly."

Pro 2:6 — "For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding."

Jas 1:5 — "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him."

Jer 33:3 — "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not."

Modern Corruption

The 411 is information, and easily becomes the talebearer’s inside story; Scripture honors careful inquiry, forbids gossip, and points the seeker to God, who gives wisdom liberally.

expand to see more

From facts to tales. Asking for the 411 is often harmless: where the party is, when the game starts, who the new teacher is. But the phrase leans toward the inside story about a person, and that is where the talebearer lives. His words go down into the innermost parts (Pro 18:8); they wound people who are not in the room. A Christian may gather facts; he may not traffic in other people’s shame. The test is simple: is it true, is it mine to tell, and will it build up?

The better operator. The old 411 operator could only give you a number. God gives far more. Out of His mouth cometh knowledge and understanding (Pro 2:6); He gives wisdom to all who ask, liberally, and upbraideth not (Jas 1:5). His invitation is a standing number: call unto me, and I will answer thee (Jer 33:3). The young person who learns to go to God first for the 411 will need the rumor mill much less.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin informare (to give form, instruct) → information → US directory assistance 4-1-1 → late-1980s African-American slang the 411 → Mary J. Blige (1992); Scripture: Call unto me, and I will answer thee (Jer 33:3).
